Orla New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Orla, Poland

Not demolished. Orla, granted town rights in 1618 with explicit permission for free Christian and Jewish settlement, saw its Jewish community rebuild quickly after mid-17th-century wartime destruction; 1,358 Jews were registered across the town and surrounding kehilla villages by 1765, still about 70% (1,450) of roughly 2,300 residents by 1939. Germans established a ghetto in March 1942, liquidated by early November that year with deportation to Treblinka. This newer of Orla's Jewish cemeteries, established around the mid-19th century and later expanded westward in the interwar period, held executed Holocaust victims; Germans and later local residents both took tombstones for construction. A commemorative stone was added in 2019.
